input.question: Why aren't high rise office fires more common/unsurvivable?
input.ground_truth: They used to, then builders got wise to it. Now we build high rises out of concrete and glass, which don't catch on fire. We restrict how much flammable material is used on the floors of high rises and don't allow anything flammable at all in the stairwells (that's why the stairs are pretty much always barren concrete with metal railings), which makes it more difficult for the fires to spread between floors.

response.prediction: High-rise office fires are rare and generally survivable because modern buildings are designed with strict safety measures. Building codes require fire-resistant materials, automatic sprinklers, smoke detectors, and clearly marked exits to prevent fires from spreading and help people escape quickly. Stairwells and fire doors are built to block flames and smoke, while regular fire drills and emergency plans ensure occupants know how to evacuate. Fire departments also use specialized equipment to respond effectively. These layers of prevention, detection, and preparedness work together to minimize risks and protect lives, making such fires uncommon and survivable when they occur.
